scope: Observable selection, camera, contextual UI, readability, object feedback, and only directly observed animation evidence. No editor or global-agency-list benchmark.

constraints.downloadBudget: within 20MB; reused existing 1,591,579-byte JWE3 worst-quality video receipt
constraints.runtimeActions: No Unity, computer-use, or game execution in this lane
claimsExcluded: exact input causality or timing unless a source explicitly documents it
NPC animation quality when no animation is visible in the cited source

jwe3Video.boundary: These frames support perspective depth, oblique presentation, and persistent gameplay UI. They do not support exact camera controls, selection causality, easing, or follow/cancel timing.

verifiedObservations: World left-click can select a visible team or a facility pick volume; a pending support request can then resolve against a clicked target.
The panel exposes support buttons, team rows, follow, cancel, and return controls, but the panel is a single agency dispatch surface rather than a compact building-owned action card.
Generic team task requests still map actions to fixed locations (concourse or exit), so the clicked facility is not yet the primary task context for ordinary team actions.

actionableCorrections.title: Make the clicked facility the sole context anchor for support actions
actionableCorrections.change: On facility pick, keep the normal city camera, show a compact facility card at the clicked building, and bind support buttons to that facility's targetId. Preserve the existing agency/team panel as a secondary detail state opened from the card.
actionableCorrections.acceptance: Click a rendered facility in the city view; the card names that facility, shows only compatible support actions, and a request records that facility target without opening a global agency list or editor.
actionableCorrections.basis: Age IV selected-context building information and site-menu behavior; Cities II building-specific UI claim.

actionableCorrections.title: Separate selection feedback from agency roster density
actionableCorrections.change: Use a short building-owned header (name, availability, current incident/support state) with 2-3 primary buttons; move team rows, follow, cancel, and return into a deliberate secondary expansion after the user chooses a support action.
actionableCorrections.seam: MvpAgencyDispatchView panel construction and Update layout
actionableCorrections.acceptance: The selected building and the next available action remain readable over the city view at the existing camera scale; no action depends on scanning a long agency/team list.
actionableCorrections.basis: OpenRCT2 persistent viewport/tool grouping and Age IV selected building panel.

actionableCorrections.title: Add a verified visual state loop before making animation claims
actionableCorrections.change: Instrument and capture three runtime states for the same facility: selected/available, request accepted/team en route, and on-site/complete. Keep camera focus and target highlight visible in each receipt; treat team motion as unknown until observed.
actionableCorrections.seam: MvpAgencyDispatchController mission states; MvpAgencyDispatchView; Station target/highlight rendering; existing evidence receipt workflow
actionableCorrections.acceptance: A fresh local receipt links each state to a frame and event log entry; no claim about easing, follow, or NPC animation is made without the corresponding observation.
actionableCorrections.basis: JWE3 frames establish a useful visual baseline only; source manuals establish state/UI concepts, not CHOOGuard runtime behavior.

decision.rationale: The strongest cross-source signal is selected-world context plus a small contextual action surface. Camera and animation details remain evidence-limited, so the first implementation increment should improve target/action binding and readable feedback before visual polish.
decision.notAcceptance: This graph is a source-grounded interaction benchmark and does not establish product acceptance, emergency procedure validity, or runtime animation quality.
